subject: Banking
title: Spoofing: Ghost Orders
description: A short lesson to help you apply Spoofing: Ghost Orders.

hook.text: JPMorgan traders placed millions of fake orders they never intended to fill.

buildup.text: Spoofing means placing large buy or sell orders to create the appearance of demand.

discovery.text: JPMorgan's precious metals desk spoofed markets for 8 years.

twist.text: JPMorgan paid $920 million and admitted to criminal conduct. It was the largest spoofing penalty in history.

climax.text: Spoofing is market manipulation using ghosts. Orders that were never real moved prices affecting real people.

punchline.text: $920 million fine. 8 years of fake orders. Ghost trades moved real prices.

quiz.question: What is 'spoofing' in financial markets?
options: Placing fake orders to move prices then canceling before execution
